input.standardization: Feature-wise mean and population standard deviation fitted on DEV_TRAIN windows only and applied unchanged to DEV_VAL

encoder.reason_for_reuse: Exact Stage 24B encoder reuse isolates the aggregation bottleneck

statistics_rationale.mean: location and dense gradient to every valid instance
statistics_rationale.standard_deviation: dispersion and dense gradient to every valid instance
statistics_rationale.q10: lower-tail behaviour without an unstable minimum
statistics_rationale.maximum: isolated extreme retained because Stage 16/24 evidence makes extremes relevant

excluded_statistics.minimum: q10 already represents the lower tail and minimum is more sensitive to one window
excluded_statistics.skewness_and_kurtosis: unstable in short bags and unnecessary for the bounded hypothesis
excluded_statistics.additional_quantiles: would create an unprincipled aggregation search
excluded_statistics.covariance: would greatly expand the representation and test a different joint-distribution hypothesis
excluded_statistics.attention: would confound distribution preservation with learned reweighting

exact_implementation.standard_deviation: sqrt(population_variance + 1e-8); the same epsilon-stabilized definition is used by the direct control
exact_implementation.quantiles: For each valid bag and latent dimension, torch.sort embeddings; at position u=q*(m-1), linearly interpolate sorted[floor(u)] and sorted[ceil(u)] for q in {0.10,0.50,0.90}
exact_implementation.maximum: Last value of the valid sorted embedding
exact_implementation.single_instance_bag: mean/q10/median/q90/maximum equal the sole embedding; stabilized standard deviation equals 1e-4
exact_implementation.padding: Invalid rows are removed before sorting/statistics and cannot affect values or gradients

differentiability.explanation: torch.sort and indexed linear interpolation are piecewise differentiable with gradients routed to the selected order statistics. Rank/order changes and ties are nondifferentiable boundaries, as with max pooling, but autograd supplies valid local subgradients. Mean and stabilized standard deviation provide dense gradients to all valid instances, so encoder learning does not depend only on sparse quantile gradients.

customer_classifier.reason: Keep the experiment about representation rather than head capacity

chronology.reason: Test distribution representation only; no sequence model or positional input
